title: Searching for Privacy Risks in LLM Agents via Simulation
bench: own:privacy-simulation (Testing-5 train / Testing-100 test; privacy norms sampled from PrivacyLens, configs generated by o4-mini-high + manual curation); own:Outlook sim-to-real case study (gpt-5.1 in ChatGPT Atlas)
evidence: judge=SELF: defense is purely an instruction in the data-sender agent (D0->D1 rule-based consent verification->D2 'strict state machine', 'verify the sender's identity at each step, and reaching out to the data subject if necessary'); no separate guard. judge_exposed=Y: sender reads attacker-agent messages/notifications. adaptive=2: search alternates attack and defense optimization 'Attack search phase: (A_T, D_T) => (A_{T+1}, D_T)' with LLM optimizer (gemini-pro) so attacks (impersonation, consent forgery) are optimized against the defended agent; after D2 'hard to find an effective A3 that further increases the leakage' (attacker LLM not told defense explicitly). 6 defender backbones (gpt-4.1-mini/4.1/4.1-nano, gemini flash, qwen3-32B, gpt-oss-20B). utility: helpful action rate on benign chit-chat D1 88.5%/D2 31.2% (recoverable to 96.2%); no cost/overhead numbers; confirm frequency not measured. public_bench=N because only norm seeds come from PrivacyLens (own test configs) - borderline.

title: Cowpox: Towards the Immunity of VLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
bench: AdvBench (malicious outputs for inspector eval; benign from chat history); own:AgentSmith-style infectious-jailbreak VLM multi-agent env (N=128 agents, kappa=4 Cowpox agents); LLaVA-Bench scored by GPT-4o (utility)
evidence: judge=SEP: 'we introduce an LLM as the inspector' (same LLaVA VLM, prompt template) that 'scores the response of the output to decide if it contains malicious content'; input = 'the answers of the COWPOX agents' (agent outputs, derived) so judge_input=DERIVED, judge_exposed=N under Y-iff-RAW rule. ML: cure sample wins CLIP RAG retrieval score vs virus sample (embedding similarity); response detected after it occurs, memory album then replaced 'Replace x_v with c' (modify, not block of the current response). adaptive=2: 'we assume the attacker is aware of the strategies of COWPOX... able to obtain the cure sample... the attacker continues the optimization on the cure sample in order to achieve a higher RAG score than the cure sample' (gradient-based; inspector LLM itself not attacked). fpr: inspector 1-turn ACC 84.7 FPR 2.8 FNR 12.5; 3-turn ACC 89.1 FPR 7.9 FNR 3.0. models: LLaVA-1.5-7B main; heterogeneous exp adds InstructBLIP (RAG encoders CLIP, DINOv2). No time/token overhead reported.

title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
bench: SHADE-Arena (17 task pairs, AgentDojo-based, public); own:CUA-SHADE-Arena (15 task pairs on TheAgentCompany, computer-use)
evidence: judge=SEP: monitor LLM (Claude 3.5 Sonnet main; weak monitor Claude 3.6 Haiku in weak-to-strong exp) outputs a suspiciousness score; 'we focus on offline monitoring: the monitor inspects the complete agent trajectory' (post-hoc, no blocking; online deployment only future work). judge_input=RAW: baseline prompt 'Here is the transcript of the agent...' with CoT, actions and tool calls/outputs (tool-output inclusion inferred from appendix prompt/trajectory description; CUA tasks include bash/file/code execution results). adaptive=1: red-team agents with awareness levels ('Aware: knows its behavior will be inspected'); hand-written strategies monitor hijacking ('inject instructions into their trajectories to manipulate the output of the monitor'), lying with jailbreaking, CoT obfuscation ('two blocks of CoTs'), dealer's choice; no iterative optimization loop described. Agents: Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 4 Sonnet. Metrics AUC and TPR@FPR=0.01 (FPR operating point = fpr Y). overhead: hierarchical monitor '~67x more computationally efficient' than baseline. HiLT case study: escalating pre-flagged cases gave ~+15% TPR at FPR=0.01; number of reviewers/time not reported (hitl_burden=N). decisions are score/flag + human escalation only.

title: Explainable and Fine-Grained Safeguarding of LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Bi-Level Graph Anomaly Detection
bench: InjecAgent (tool attack, TA-InjecAgent); PoisonRAG (MA-PoisonRAG); CSQA, MMLU, GSM8K prompt-injection setups (following G-Safeguard/BlindGuard settings); topologies chain/tree/star/random
evidence: judge=ML: XG-Guard = GNN encoder + prototype-based unsupervised anomaly detector over SentenceBERT sentence/token embeddings of agent responses and the communication graph; 'No LLM participates in the detection decision' (judge_exposed=-, judge_input=-). Detected agents isolated by 'pruning both the inward and outward edges' (limit); detection per dialogue round, isolation protects later rounds only. adaptive=0: no adaptive/stealthy attacker; Limitations only mention domain breadth and API model drift; 'defense budget is set to three' (top-3 anomalous agents always flagged). Backbones: GPT-4o-mini main; DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-30B-A3B only on CSQA and PoisonRAG. ACC = task performance after defense (utility Y). Overhead only asymptotic 'O(NL^2+M)', no measured time/tokens; no benign-only false-alarm evaluation.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Protecting LLM Agents Against Tool Description Poisoning via Isolated Planning
bench: AgentDojo (97 tasks, 76 tools; Banking/Slack/Travel/Workspace; ~40% of tools poisoned); ASB (10 scenarios, 400+ tools)
evidence: judge=SEP;RULE: two LLM validators per candidate call - Align(u, validated prior actions, a_t) sees only user intent + validated progress, Susp(u, m_t, a_t) 'uses the full context (including prior tool outputs)' (judge_input=RAW, judge_exposed=Y); tool descriptions excluded from validation; on failure the tool is moved to the 'Influenced' list (descriptions withheld from planner) and re-planned (max 3 attempts); deterministic Choose rule; partition derived from LLM validation at runtime (policy_src=LLM). pre-execution validation before each tool call. adaptive=2: 'adversary knows the defense details'; semantic-adaptive (alignment-/suspicion-adaptive fake justification, level 1) plus 'PAIR ... and TAP ... black-box, iterative LLM jailbreaking' to 'iteratively optimize the poisoned tool description' with feedback from defended agent; ASR PAIR 2.06%, TAP 0.00%, semantic variants 0. Models: AgentDojo 5 LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-pro, Gemini-2.5-flash, Claude-3.5-haiku) + ASB 5 LLMs (GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o-2024-05-13, GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-3.5-turbo) = 7 distinct families (8 snapshots). Overhead: ~1.45x/1.39x tokens (abstract says 0.5x increase), 3.7x runtime, 2 planning + 2 validation LLM calls/step. Benign utility reported (e.g. GPT-4o-mini 68.04%); no explicit FPR (fpr=N). No user confirmation.

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
bench: own:calendar scheduling; own:expense-report compilation; own:collaborative blog writing (no public security benchmark)
evidence: judge=RULE only: central Provider + cryptographic one-time access-control tokens (OTK) and user-written 'Access Contact Policy' (manual pattern-matching rules with scores/budgets; 'The Provider verifies that B is in A's contact policy'); no LLM in enforcement (judge_exposed=-); controls who may initiate agent-to-agent connections and token expiry/request quota ('limit on the number of permitted requests'), not per-tool actions or message content ('SAGA can be used in conjunction with defenses against prompt-injection'). adaptive=1 (borderline): attacker models A1-A8 (invalid TLS, missing/expired token, impersonation, token reuse across agents, policy violation, unauthorized registration, valid-token abuse) are protocol-specific; 'we implemented these attacker models in our evaluation' but only qualitative results (Table II: step at which each attack is detected); no optimizing/defense-feedback attacker; would be 0 if only defense-aware adaptive attackers count. Backbones: GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1, Qwen-2.5-72B. utility: 'all agents successfully complete their tasks' (qualitative). Overhead: <25 ms amortized/request, <0.6% of calendar task end-to-end time. No FPR, no user study; user involvement only at registration/policy authoring.

title: AttriGuard: Defeating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Causal Attribution of Tool Invocations
bench: AgentDojo (92 user tasks, 882 attack instances); ASB (400 attack instances); static attacks IGNOREPREVIOUS, COMBINED, IMPORTANTMESSAGES, TOOLKNOWLEDGE
evidence: judge=RULE;SEP: gating of each proposed tool call by parallel counterfactual 'shadow replay' run by the agent LLM on a 'control-attenuated view of external observations' (LLM-based rewriting by flattening, perspective rewriting, causal weakening - so LLMs read raw untrusted observations: judge_exposed=Y, policy_src=LLM because the allowed call set = shadow candidates); steps: function-name match, exact argument match, then 'auxiliary LLM judge that takes T_u, the proposed call c, and the candidates' (no observation text: judge_input=DERIVED). Block = 'returning an empty tool result with an injection warning'. adaptive=2: 'adapted from ... Nasr et al.' MAP-Elites controller + mutator 'explicitly condition[ed] on ... the deployed defense and a structured summary of the agent's runtime defense state'; adversary 'has complete knowledge of the agent system and the deployed defense'; 200 (and 500) queries per instance; AttriGuard adaptive ASR 6.56% (Gemini-2.5), 9.84% (Llama3.3) vs baselines up to 82%. Models: Gemini-2.5 Flash, GPT-4.1-mini, Qwen3-32B, Llama3.3-70B. Overhead ~2x tokens, 32-41 s latency (~3x undefended). Utility ~3% drop; no explicit FPR (Llama3.3 Travel -20% utility). User confirmation only as future mitigation (hitl '-').

title: Enhancing LLM Agent Safety via Causal Influence Prompting
bench: MobileSafetyBench (incl. 10 indirect-prompt-injection tasks); RedCode-Exec; AgentHarm (jailbreak-template attack)
evidence: judge=SELF: the agent LLM itself builds a causal influence diagram (CID) from task instruction + action space, prepends it as text, and 'reasons about how it can act more safely' before each action; CID refined each step from 'the previous CID, the current action, and the current observation' (reads untrusted observations: judge_exposed=Y; Limitations: 'if the backbone LLM in CIP is susceptible to indirect prompt injection, it may generate an incorrect CID'). Agent can call ask-consent() (HUMAN; frequency/burden not measured: hitl N). adaptive=0: only existing attacks - indirect prompt injection in observations and 'rule-based jailbreak template from Andriushchenko et al. (2024a) with minor modification'; nothing designed against CIP. Models GPT-4o, Gemini-1.5-Pro, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, Qwen2.5-72B (Qwen excluded from AgentHarm). Utility: low-risk goal achievement drop up to 14% (consent requested before reading messages). Overhead: 'approximately a threefold increase in the cost of generating a single action' (CIP $0.027 vs CoT $0.0086/action, MobileSafetyBench). No separate over-refusal/FPR metric.

title: AdvEvo-MARL: Shaping Internalized Safety through Adversarial Co-Evolution in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
bench: NetSafe (official dataset); AutoInject and UserHijack with 300-prompt pool sampled from JailbreakBench, WildJailbreak, StrongREJECT; utility: AIME'24/'25, LiveCodeBench v6, GPQA-diamond
evidence: judge=SELF: 'Rather than relying on external guards', safety is internalized in task agents by MARL (REINFORCE++) co-evolution of attacker and defender agents; no guard at inference (an external 'Inspector' agent is only a baseline). judge_exposed=Y: defenders read injected inter-agent messages / hijacked user instructions. adaptive=0 (flag): the co-evolved attacker ('synthesize evolving jailbreak prompts') is optimized against the defender during training only; evaluation uses fixed attack pools ('we construct a 300 adversarial prompts pool by sampling JailbreakBench, Wild Jailbreak, and Strong Reject'), no GCG/PAIR or post-hoc adaptive attacker reported; text does not state explicitly whether test-time prompts come from evolved attackers. Models: Qwen2.5-3B and 7B (2 trained); GPT-3.5/GPT-4o-mini are comparison baselines. Utility: max ~3% drop at 3B; 7B improves. No overhead, over-refusal/FPR, or human confirmation reported.

title: Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Corruptions via Node Contribution Backpropagation
bench: own:MAS setups on MMLU, Alpaca, SamSum, ChatDoctor with 5 attack types (harmful, suboptimal, reframing, trigger, modification); flat 5 agents x 3 rounds and hierarchy [5,2,5]
evidence: judge=SEP;RULE: Backward Propagation Detection - an independent LLM scorer rates each message pair g_ij=f(s_i,s_j) in {-1,0,1} (contradiction/low/positive contribution; prompt 'an advisor has responded to an assistant... agrees') on raw inter-agent message text (judge_input=RAW, judge_exposed=Y); contributions backpropagated on a signed DAG and agents flagged by deterministic outlier threshold (statistical threshold, policy_src='-'); mitigation 'Remove all outgoing messages from agents' (limit); detection/repair is per query, applied after run (pruning for subsequent communication). adaptive=1: 'System-Aware (SA) adaptive attack' where 'corrupted agents are provided with detailed system information, including the global topology, the scoring mechanism, and current neighborhood scores... detector-evasive strategies, such as intermittently giving correct and incorrect answers or disrupting scores'; hand-designed, no optimization loop; BPD degrades only 3-4%. Models GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3. Overhead: 9.0%/10.6% extra time (flat/hierarchy), one scoring call per edge; tokens not reported. No explicit FPR; no-attack accuracy maintained. No human confirmation.

title: MINIM: Privacy-Aware Minimal View for Agents via Trusted Local Sanitization
src: https://arxiv.org/html/2606.13949 (ICML 2026 camera-ready text; version not shown)
bench: own:privacy-augmented WebArena-derived corpus (150 accessibility trees, 27 task types, 5,403 variants, 662 test; Shopping/Reddit/Gmail; synthetic 2FA codes/passwords/notifications injected)
evidence: judge=ML;RULE: trusted local broker with a GATv2 model (3 layers) predicting per-UI-node sensitivity and task-conditioned necessity, then fixed ternary policy Keep/Abstract/Remove by manual thresholds ('administrators can adjust tau post-deployment'); no LLM at runtime (judge_exposed=-, judge_input=-); abstraction = rule-based [REDACTED] masking. Applied to accessibility-tree observations before leaving the device (stage I). adversarial=Y but only passive: remote model is 'honest-but-curious... passively harvesting task-irrelevant content'; 'We do not consider active adversaries that attempt to manipulate the agent via prompt injection'; adaptive=0: no adversarial/evasion evaluation (only '>99.9% of injected 2FA codes... suppressed' diagnostic). n_models=0: no end-to-end agent LLM run; 6 LLMs (Qwen3-8B, Nemotron-Nano-9B, Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-3-8B, Mistral-7B, Gemma-3N) only as baseline scorers. utility=N: only node-level proxies TCNP 0.9491, TCNP-I 0.9931, TISL 0.101, Keep rate ~12%; no task-success, latency or FPR reported.

title: Building a Foundational Guardrail for General Agentic Systems via Synthetic Data
bench: own:Pre-Exec Bench (1,672 samples: 1,001 harmless/671 harmful; built on Agent-SafetyBench scenarios/tools, human verified); case study on MetaGPT and AutoGen with human-injected risks
evidence: judge=SEP: Safiron, a compact 8B guardian LLM (Ministral-8B, SFT+RL) trained on AuraGen synthetic data; input = user query + environment/tool info + the agent's planned action trajectory 'in the planning stage... has not yet executed them' (planned tool invocations; no observations/tool outputs: judge_input=DERIVED, judge_exposed=N); outputs binary risk, risk category, explanation; paper does not specify block vs confirm deployment (decisions=block assumed). Threat model: 'Malicious actors can exploit these systems, and agents themselves may generate harmful action sequences'; risk categories include external attacks, but no adversarial/adaptive evaluation (adaptive=0). n_models=8: planner LLMs used to generate Pre-Exec Bench plans (Qwen2.5-72B, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-R1, Llama-3.3-70B, Llama-4-Maverick, Qwen3-32B, Mixtral-8x22B, gpt-oss-20B); the guard itself is one model; case-study backbones unnamed. 11 baseline guard/LLM models compared. Metrics: accuracy 94.9%, harmful precision 97.3%, category 64.6%, explanation 57.0%; no FPR or benign-task utility. Throughput 33 samples/s (8xH100). public_bench=N: derived from Agent-SafetyBench but evaluated only on own bench.
